summary: Edward Upham (1776-1834) worked in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He was a fellow of the Society of Antiquaries of London and served as a member of the Royal Asiatic Society from circa 1823 to 1834.

Edward Vernon Arnold (1857-1926) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell and at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. He was a fellow at Trinity College, Cambridge, and served as professor at Bangor University (1884-1924).
Edward W. Said (1935-2003) studied at Princeton University and Harvard University. From circa 1963 to 2003, he held an academic post in English and Comparative Literature at Columbia University.

Edward Washburn Hopkins (1857-1932) studied at Columbia and Leipzig under Albrecht Weber and Ernst Windisch. An Indologist and linguist, he taught at Bryn Mawr (1885-1895) before serving as professor at Yale (1895-1926) and editing the Journal of the American Oriental Society.

Edward William West (1824-1905) was an Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological scholar. He studied at King's College London (1839-1842) under Duncan Forbes and later studied under Martin Haug between 1867 and 1873.

Edward Winslow Bastian is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, Geshe Lobsang, Geshe Lobsang Donyo, and Lobsang Tenzin.

Edward Winter Clark (1830-1913) was a linguist who studied at Brown University, Newton Theological Institution, and Colgate Rochester Crozer Divinity School. He served as a missionary with the American Baptist Missionary Union from 1869 to 1911.

Edwin Abbott Abbott (1838-1926) studied at the City of London School and St John's College. He held teaching posts at St John's College, King Edward's School, Clifton College, and served at the City of London School from 1865 to 1889.

Edwin Arnold (1832-1904) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Japanology after studying at King's College London and Oxford. He served as principal of Deccan College (1856-1861), taught at Keio University, and founded the Maha Bodhi Society.

Edwin Capers Kirkland (1902-1972) worked in Indology and earned his Ph.D. from Northwestern University. He held an academic post at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville (~1934-1946) and became Professor of English at the University of Florida in 1946.

Edwin Felix Thomas Atkinson (1840-1890) was an Indology and history scholar who studied at Trinity College Dublin. He served as President of The Asiatic Society (1886-1887) and as Accountant General for the Government of Bengal.

Edwin Francis Bryant (born 1957) is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned his doctorate from Columbia University in 1997. He taught at Harvard University (~1998-2001) and became Associate Professor of Hinduism at Rutgers University circa 2001.

Edwin Gerow (1931-2023) studied Indology and philosophy under J. A. B. van Buitenen, Louis Renou, George V. Bobrinskoy, and V. Ranganathan. He held posts at the University of Washington, Reed College (1985-2002), and edited the Journal of the American Oriental Society.

Edwin Greaves (1854-1941) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Western College (~1876-1881). He served as a London Missionary Society missionary (~1881-1920) and principal of both the LMS College in Benares and the Missionary Language School in Lucknow.

Edwin Hotchkiss Tuttle (1879-1939) worked in linguistics and Indology. After studying at Yale University from circa 1897 to 1901, he held positions as a language teacher at the Mackenzie School and the Boys' Latin School of Maryland.

Edwin Lee Johnson (1874-1947), a scholar of linguistics and Indology, studied at the University of Mississippi and Vanderbilt University. He taught at Quitman College and Alexander Institute before becoming Professor of Latin and Greek at Vanderbilt in 1935.

Edwin Möhrke (died 1960) was an Indologist who studied philology at the University of Marburg in 1923. He later completed his Ph.D. at the University of Königsberg under Helmuth von Glasenapp in 1934.

Edwin Norris (1795-1872) was a scholar in linguistics, history, archaeology, and Indology. He held posts at the East India Company, the Foreign Office, and the Royal Asiatic Society, where he served as assistant secretary and journal editor.

Edwin Whitfield Fay (1865-1920) studied linguistics and Indology at Rhodes College, Johns Hopkins, and Leipzig under Karl Brugmann and Ernst Windisch. He taught at Michigan, Washington and Lee (1893-1899), and was Professor of Latin at the University of Texas.

Egaku Maeda (1926-2010) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his doctorate at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji, Shoson Miyamoto, Hajime Nakamura, and Kogen Mizuno. He was later a professor at Aichi Gakuin University (1972-2002).
